red_team.case_for_morning: The series is noisy and moved 3 points in one day (19→22, 11→12 Nov). Weekend demand peaks and lags in station declarations could add 5 points; barges reach depots days after the Rhine gauge rises.
red_team.case_further: Three readings in a row fell (22→19→18) while France dropped to 8%; the Rhine is back to normal on forecast, pointing to about 14–16% by Saturday 17h; 0.03 may still be too high.
red_team.why: The morning 59% rested on a rising trend that has reversed on two official readings, and its cause, the low Rhine, is easing on schedule. No new shock found.
red_team.factor: outcome (slip_class none; p_held unchanged, Saturday publication still a void risk only)
red_team.likeliest_failure: A new shock before Saturday 17h: depot blockade or strike, panic buying or slow barge deliveries.

red_team.case_for_morning: Every new fact was scheduled and expected from the 7 Nov target; the real hurdle, the FAA licence, is still unlisted on launch morning; scrubs cluster on launch day; the raw finals (0.63) are below the morning figure and only calibration lifts them to 0.73.
red_team.case_further: The window runs two days, so one scrub or 24-hour slip still counts; closures are in force, weather good, nothing slipped 11 hours before T-0; past licences arrived in the last day; 0.78–0.80 is defensible.
